title: A Preregistered Paired Evaluation of Generate–Verify–Repair (GVR) for Intent→Configuration NetOps: Null Results on a Synthetic Verifier-Checked Task Bank
abstract: We report a fully preregistered paired experiment that tested whether a deterministic verifier plus a bounded LLM-guided repair loop (Generate–Verify–Repair, GVR) reduces verifier-detected semantic invariant violations for intent→device-configuration translation. The confirmatory design used a public synthetic NetOps task bank (N = 240 paired tasks), a single generator pairing (gpt-5-mini), and a pybatfish-style deterministic validator. Execution used shared-initial-candidate semantics (one generated candidate per task reused across arms) and allowed at most one bounded repair attempt per task. All planned episodes completed (planned_episode_count = 480; completed_episode_count = 480) with a single generation per task (model_calls_used = 240). Every generated candidate satisfied the deterministic verifier in both arms: n11 = 240, n10 = n01 = n00 = 0. The paired estimate (rate_GVR − rate_baseline) = 0.0; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00; paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729). Two preregistration/execution issues constrain inference: (1) the executed shared-generation semantics removed independent per-arm stochasticity assumed in the preregistered power calculation, and (2) a prespecified comparison against a schema-constrained baseline was not executed. Conservatively interpreted, bounded GVR produced no verifier-detectable benefit in this specific, artifact-grounded setting because there were no verifier-detectable errors to correct. We publish authoritative archived artifacts and recommend reproducible follow-ups that restore per-condition generation, include adversarial/golden tasks, broaden generator families, and expand verifier coverage.

sections.introduction:
Automating intent→device-configuration translation with large language models (LLMs) promises efficiency but raises operational safety concerns: stochastic generators can emit syntactically plausible yet semantically incorrect commands that violate network invariants (reachability, workflow ordering, or security predicates). Prior work therefore recommends pipelines that interpose deterministic validators and iterative repair (generate–verify–repair, GVR) to detect and correct mechanically checkable defects prior to execution. We asked a focused operational question suitable for a preregistered confirmatory test: under a frozen design that used a single generator/prompt pairing and shared-initial-candidate generation semantics, does inserting a deterministic verifier plus a bounded LLM-guided repair loop reduce verifier-detected semantic invariant violations relative to an unconstrained baseline? We preregistered estimands, froze the analysis executor, archived all artifacts, and executed the run without manual post-lock manuscript edits.

Contributions. (1) A fully preregistered, artifact-backed paired evaluation on a public synthetic NetOps task bank (240 paired tasks) using a single generator (gpt-5-mini) and a pybatfish-style deterministic validator. (2) Transparent execution accounting showing shared-initial-candidate semantics (one generation per task reused across arms), model_calls_used = 240, and complete scoring artifacts. (3) Confirmatory statistics reporting a degenerate null (n11 = 240; paired estimate = 0.0; exact McNemar p = 1.00; paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0]) together with a concise reconciliation of preregistered power assumptions and executed semantics. (4) A compact evidence-to-claim mapping and a nearest-work comparison matrix (both artifact-grounded) and reproducible recommendations for follow-up evaluations that restore discordance potential and adversarial sensitivity.
sections.related_work:
We position this experiment in three convergent literatures. First, studies of hallucination and fabrication in LLM outputs for code and structured artifacts show that unconstrained generation can produce incorrect, non-executable, or unsafe outputs, motivating deterministic validators in downstream pipelines. Representative sources (surveys and empirical studies) document these phenomena and motivate verify stages. Second, generate–verify–repair and constrained-decoding techniques (e.g., grammar- or schema-constrained decoding) improve syntactic/executable properties and reduce surface hallucinations; case studies report improvements for mechanically checkable properties but leave semantic-invariant guarantees open. Third, NetOps-specific research emphasizes verifier-driven evaluation (reachability/policy invariants), intent-based translation systems, and human-in-the-loop governance as controls for high-stakes changes.

Nearest-work comparison matrix (selected entries from the archived bibliography). Each row lists the closest prior study and one-line contrast to the present run.

- NetConfEval (Wang et al., 2024): benchmarked LLMs on configuration tasks; differs by being a broad open benchmark rather than a preregistered paired confirmatory study with a deterministic verifier.

- Confucius (Wang et al., 2025): intent-driven multi-agent NetOps framework emphasizing verification; differs by architecture/prototype focus and not reporting an archived paired preregistered GVR confirmatory test.

- MeshAgent (Zhou et al., 2025): system-level effort to enable reliable LLM management with validators; differs in deployment scope and not formal preregistered paired testing of bounded repair efficacy.

- Grammar-constrained decoding (Tuccio et al., 2025): improves syntactic validity via grammar constraints; differs because syntactic gains do not guarantee domain semantic invariant improvements measured here.

- Generate-Verify-Repair methodology (Cadenas, 2026): proposes GVR architectures for deterministic validation; our work implements a preregistered, paired test of a bounded GVR intervention under narrow execution semantics.

This run extends prior work by combining preregistration, a paired confirmatory estimand, deterministic analysis executor, and artifact-backed accounting; it differs from exploratory or benchmark studies by its confirmatory intent and frozen analysis pipeline.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study was preregistered under an archived preregistration record that specified the primary estimand as the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (proportion difference in verifier-detected semantic violations in paired tasks). Two prespecified primary comparisons were listed: (C vs A) GVR vs unconstrained generation and (C vs B) GVR vs schema-constrained decoding with Bonferroni correction (family alpha = 0.05 → per-comparison alpha = 0.025). The analysis executor 'paired_binary_analysis_v1' and all analysis code were frozen before execution.

Design and execution contract. Confirmatory sample: N = 240 tasks (12 topology/policy clusters × 20 tasks per cluster). Execution used a shared-initial-candidate semantics: the generator produced one initial candidate per task that was reused for both scored conditions; maximum allowed repair attempts per task = 1 (bounded single repair). The requested generator was gpt-5-mini; deterministic validation used a pybatfish-style deterministic_netops_validator implementation. The adapter/orchestration family that executed the run is archived.

Task bank, oracle, and scoring. The synthetic task bank encodes initial states, intents, workflow constraints, and expected final states; the deterministic validator returns structured diagnostics (violation_count, violations list, parsed_command_count, required_command_count). Scoring rule: full_intent_constraint_validation implemented by deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Representative task manifests and scoring JSONs (per-task validator_trace blocks) are archived and authoritative for recorded scores.

Analysis plan. The preregistered primary comparisons were to be evaluated with a paired exact McNemar-style test and paired-bootstrap confidence intervals (paired_bootstrap_percentile; 10,000 resamples). The preregistered power calculation assumed independent per-condition generation; that assumption is discussed below because the executed design used shared-generation semantics, which deterministically affects discordance potential and invalidates the preregistered power assumption for the executed run.

Compact evidence-to-claim mapping. For transparency, we map principal empirical claims to the archived artifacts (paths shown; full hash manifest and complete artifact hashes are available in the archived execution manifest). Key mappings:

- "All planned episodes completed; modeling calls used = 240; shared-generation semantics": execution/execution_manifest.json and execution/model_configuration.json and execution/raw_results.jsonl.

- "Every generated candidate satisfied the deterministic verifier (n11 = 240)": analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/condition_summary.csv and execution/scoring/*.json (representative examples execution/scoring/task-000001-*.json).

- "No repairs were applied (repair_applied = false for all episodes)": execution/scoring/*.json validator_trace blocks and execution/responses/*.

- "Analysis outputs (exact McNemar p = 1.00; paired-bootstrap CI = [0.0,0.0])": analysis/results.json and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl.

Readers may consult execution/execution_manifest.json (archived manifest) for the full hash manifest and provenance details; the manifest contains the authoritative file-level hashes and a reproducible file list.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. The execution manifest records planned_episode_count = 480, completed_episode_count = 480, failed_episode_count = 0, and model_calls_used = 240 under shared-initial-candidate semantics. Deterministic reconciliation artifacts confirm episode accounting and provider-call audit details.

Primary outcomes. The paired contingency observed was n11 = 240 (both arms accepted), n10 = 0 (guarded only), n01 = 0 (baseline only), n00 = 0 (both rejected). Summary rates: baseline_success_rate = 1.0; guarded_success_rate = 1.0; paired estimate (rate_GVR − rate_baseline) = 0.0. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00. Paired-bootstrap 95% CI (paired_bootstrap_percentile; 10,000 resamples; bootstrap_seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.0]. These numbers and the per-task records are archived (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, execution/scoring/*.json).

Repair usage and trigger diagnostics. For every episode the validator trace shows repair_applied = false; the bounded repair loop never executed because the shared initial candidate satisfied validator predicates for every task. Representative per-task scoring JSONs (execution/scoring/task-000001-*.json) record validator validation_before and validation_after blocks with violation_count = 0.

Statistical interpretation. The observed contingency (no discordant pairs) yields a degenerate paired test: there are no within-pair disagreements from which to estimate a differential effect. The exact-test p = 1.00 and the bootstrap CI collapsing to [0.0, 0.0] are deterministic consequences of the observed contingency and the preregistered analysis procedures. The preregistered power calculation assumed independent per-condition generation; because execution used shared-generation semantics (one candidate reused across arms), that power calculation does not apply to this executed design.
sections.discussion:
Conservative interpretation and mechanisms. The artifact-backed null result demonstrates that, under the executed shared-initial-candidate semantics and for the supplied synthetic workload and validator predicates, a bounded GVR intervention (one allowed repair) produced no verifier-detectable benefit because the generator+prompting pairing already produced verifier-acceptable outputs for every task. Two non-exclusive mechanisms supported by archived artifacts explain the outcome: (1) task/verifier alignment — the synthetic task bank, generator prompt, and deterministic validator together defined a distribution the generator could satisfy deterministically; (2) sensitivity reduction from shared-generation semantics — reusing one candidate across arms removes independent stochastic variation and therefore removes within-pair discordance that GVR could exploit.

Implications for evaluation practice. To evaluate whether GVR reduces verifier-detected violations under generator stochasticity, the experimental semantics must allow independent per-condition generation (independent_condition_generation = true), include adversarial or golden-reference tasks to exercise verifier sensitivity, or test multiple generator families and prompt variants. The archived artifacts contain the task manifest, RNG seeds, and adapter configuration that permit deterministic reruns under alternative generation semantics; the full hash manifest in the archived execution manifest documents the files needed for deterministic reproduction.

Threats to validity (concise). Internal validity: mismatch between preregistered power assumptions (independent generation) and executed shared-generation semantics. Construct validity: deterministic validator encodes a subset of operational invariants; passing the validator does not guarantee absence of all real-world risks. External validity: single generator (gpt-5-mini), synthetic task bank, bounded single-repair budget. Conclusion validity: zero discordant outcomes preclude evidence for GVR efficacy under executed semantics. These threats are enumerated in the archived limitations and reconciliation artifacts.

Recommendations grounded in archived artifacts. (1) Re-run the preregistered paired design with independent per-condition generation to restore discordance potential (toggle independent_condition_generation = true in the archived adapter configuration). (2) Inject adversarial or golden tasks (the preregistration planned golden-reference injections) whose expected verifier outcomes are known to validate verifier sensitivity. (3) Expand generator scope beyond gpt-5-mini and increase the repair budget (allow multiple repair iterations and record iteration distributions). (4) Broaden verifier coverage (additional semantic invariants or formal/SMT hybrids) to reduce oracle incompleteness risk. The archived run contains the deterministic seeds, task manifest, and adapter configuration needed to perform these reproducible follow-ups.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered, artifact-archived paired experiment evaluating a bounded GVR intervention on a synthetic intent→configuration NetOps task bank. Under the executed shared-initial-candidate semantics (one shared generation per task reused across arms), every generated candidate satisfied the deterministic validator (n11 = 240) and the paired estimate was 0.0 (exact McNemar p = 1.00; paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0]). Conservatively interpreted, bounded GVR provided no verifier-detectable value in this specific, artifact-grounded setting because there were no verifier-detectable errors to correct. However, two procedural factors materially constrain inference: (1) the executed shared-generation semantics invalidated the preregistered independent-generation power assumption, and (2) a prespecified schema-constrained-baseline comparison (C vs B) was not executed. We do not generalize beyond the specific model, prompt, task bank, verifier, repair budget, or generation semantics. We publish the authoritative archived artifacts to enable deterministic reruns and recommend follow-ups that restore per-condition generation and adversarial sensitivity to more robustly assess GVR’s operational value.

limitations: Synthetic task bank and verifier scope: N = 240 tasks were synthetic and evaluated against a pybatfish-style deterministic validator; results may not generalize to production topologies, vendor-specific syntax, or semantic invariants not encoded in the verifier.

Shared-generation semantics: the archived run used generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one initial generation per task reused across arms). This design reduced model-call cost but removed per-arm stochastic variation and therefore reduced sensitivity to detect GVR benefits that rely on independent per-condition generator variability; the preregistered power calculation assumed independent per-condition generation and therefore does not apply to the executed design.
Single-model evaluation: the experiment used one generator (gpt-5-mini); cross-model generality is not established.
Repair budget: only a single bounded repair iteration was permitted; different or larger repair budgets or iterative strategies might produce different outcomes.
Verifier completeness risk: passing the deterministic verifier does not guarantee absence of all operational risks (unobserved invariants or properties outside the verifier model).

Prespecified comparison not executed: the preregistration included a prespecified schema-constrained-baseline comparison (C vs B) that was not executed in the archived run; the artifacts do not record a rationale, which is an unresolved procedural limitation.
